speaker: Doctor

text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history of fatigue, flank pain, and fever after recent antibiotic treatment is highly suggestive of a kidney infection. Have you noticed any burning sensation during urination or any visible blood in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, CBC.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophilic, binucleated cells in your urine is a very specific finding that often points to an allergic reaction to medications rather than a bacterial kidney infection, despite your fever and flank pain. Given your recent antibiotic treatment for sinusitis, did you experience any hives, rash, or itching?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: That timeline of rash appearing with amoxicillin and resolving after switching to cephalexin, combined with eosinophilic cells in your urine, strongly suggests an acute drug reaction. Did you also experience itching or swelling in your lips or eyes while on the first antibiotic?
